# estilex

<!-- badges: start -->
[![R-CMD-check](https://github.com/KristianVepsalainen/estilex/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/KristianVepsalainen/estilex/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml)
<!-- badges: end -->

estilex retrieves Estonian legislation from the
[Riigi Teataja](https://www.riigiteataja.ee) public API: consolidated texts,
their structure down to subsection level, amendment histories, and English
translations aligned section by section with the Estonian original.

It is part of **lexverse**, a family of R packages for legal and regulatory
data that also includes
[eurlex](https://cran.r-project.org/package=eurlex),
[finlex](https://cran.r-project.org/package=finlex),
[swelex](https://cran.r-project.org/package=swelex) and
[danlex](https://cran.r-project.org/package=danlex).

## Installation

```r
install.packages("estilex")
```

Development version:

```r
# install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("KristianVepsalainen/estilex")
```

## Usage

A document is identified by the twelve-digit Riigi Teataja identifier that
appears in its address. The Constitution of the Republic of Estonia, in the
consolidated version in force, is `111042025003`.

```{r}
library(estilex)

doc <- etx_get_doc("111042025003")
doc$pealkiri
doc$kehtivuse_algus
```

The text arrives either whole or one provision per row:

```{r}
txt <- etx_get_text("111042025003")
nchar(txt$text)

par <- etx_get_paragraphs("111042025003")
nrow(par)
par[par$paragrahv_nr == "10", c("peatykk_pealkiri", "paragrahv", "text")]
```

Amendment history comes from the `muutmismärge` elements, which sit at two
levels in the XML: some apply to the act, others to a single section.

```{r}
ref <- etx_get_references("111042025003")
nrow(ref)
table(is.na(ref$scope_nr))
```

### Parallel texts

Estonian and English versions of an act use the same section numbering, so
they can be joined on the number rather than on position. This is what makes
estilex more than a retrieval wrapper: translation fidelity becomes
measurable.

```{r}
pp <- etx_get_parallel("111042025003")
nrow(pp)

# Where the translation is markedly shorter than the original
head(pp[!is.na(pp$text_en) & pp$n_char_en < 0.7 * pp$n_char_et,
        c("paragrahv", "n_char_et", "n_char_en")])
```

Each consolidated version is linked to the translation that corresponds to
it, not always to the newest one, so the comparison is contemporaneous. The
two validity dates are carried on every row for that reason:

```{r}
unique(pp[, c("kehtivuse_algus", "kehtivuse_algus_en")])
```

Only the Estonian text has legal force in domestic proceedings. English
translations are kept current but are not official texts, and the Riigi
Teataja holds them on a separate route for that reason. estilex follows it
automatically.

### Finding identifiers

The API has no search or enumeration endpoint. Identifiers come either from
references inside documents already retrieved, or from the open data
archives, which are downloaded on request and not by default:

```r
etx_download_corpus("en")        # about 1.1 GB across three annual archives
idx <- etx_list_documents("en")  # one row per document
etx_corpus_status()
etx_clear_corpus()
```

Archive coverage begins in 2024 and is complementary rather than
cumulative: each annual folder holds the acts published that year together
with earlier acts that received a new version during it. Acts untouched
since 2024 are absent from the archives but retrievable by identifier.

## Citing sources

Section 12 of the Riigi Teataja Act requires a reproduced text to cite the
published version. Every function returns `source_url` for that purpose.

```{r}
doc$source_url
```
